indicators.name: Weather/climate data infrastructure for agriculture

anchors.L1: No functioning agrometeorological observation network or data access.
anchors.L2: Observation infrastructure exists but agriculture-relevant forecasts are not produced reliably.
anchors.L3: Agriculture-relevant forecasts and advisories are produced with defined ownership; dissemination reaches a minority of farming households; impact-based advisories are absent.
anchors.L4: Impact-based agromet advisories are produced and disseminated through channels reaching most farming areas (radio, mobile, extension), aligned to crop calendars.
anchors.L5: End-to-end climate services: observations, impact-based forecasts and last-mile dissemination with verified reach and farmer feedback, sustained by budget and a hydromet-agriculture agreement.

indicators.calibration_note: v1.3 rewrite: anchor now tests the full climate-services chain (observation -> forecast -> last-mile reach), not data infrastructure alone.

process_ladder.name: Populate indicators
process_ladder.output: Populated workbook: 102 indicators with value, source name, source URL, year
process_ladder.guidance: Populate all 102 indicators. Quantitative indicators score themselves via the numeric-threshold rule on the Indicators sheet. Qualitative indicators are scored 1–5 by the assessor against the Qualitative Anchors sheet; the machine may propose a level, but the assessor level always wins. Every reading records source name, source URL, and observation year.

process_ladder.name: Score evidence quality
process_ladder.output: Evidence Quality Index per pillar; refresh list; verify list
process_ladder.guidance: For each reading, tag confidence High / Medium / Low / Data Gap. Staleness is automatic (year vs indicator max age). Coverage per pillar is automatic. Weighted evidence adequacy per read-out is automatic. All five feed a single Evidence Quality Index (green / amber / red) per pillar, plus two underlying lists: Refresh (stale readings + Low-confidence readings) and Verify (data gaps + unmeasured core gates).

process_ladder.name: Compile diagnostic package
process_ladder.guidance: Render the Diagnostic Package sheet: three read-outs (CMS/EMS/OES), provisional stage with caveat, core-gate audit (14 prerequisites), top binding constraints by pillar, Refresh list, Verify list, and the full 102-indicator appendix with source, year, confidence. Export as PDF. This is the single artefact handed to the TTL.

process_ladder.name: Draft the DAR offline
process_ladder.guidance: The TTL and team draft the DAR offline, after the government mandate, drawing on the Diagnostic Package as evidence. This workbook is an input to that process, not part of it. The DAR is authored, validated with the steering committee, adopted and disclosed under the DAR methodology, which is separate from this workbook.

mandate_note: The government mandate does not gate the workbook. Steps 1–3 can run on public evidence at any time and produce a diagnostic package for internal Bank use. The mandate gates the DAR: nothing is called a DAR before the government has mandated the work. The Diagnostic Package is watermarked accordingly.

glossary.name: Capability Maturity Score
glossary.text: Weighted mean of C1–C4 pillar levels (25/30/25/20). Reported 1–5.

glossary.name: Ecosystem Maturity Score
glossary.text: Weighted mean of E1 (70%) and E2 (30%) pillars.

glossary.name: Outcome & Equity Score
glossary.text: O1 pillar mean level. Deliberately kept separate from CMS/EMS.

glossary.name: Overall stage
glossary.text: Stage 1 (Foundation constrained) through Stage 5 (Transformative). Derived non-compensatively from CMS/EMS/OES subject to core-gate and coverage rules.

glossary.name: Core-gate indicator
glossary.text: 14 foundational indicators treated as prerequisites, not points. L1 caps the stage at 1; unmeasured suppresses the stage entirely.

glossary.name: Coverage gate
glossary.text: Share of a pillar's indicators that carry an assigned level. Below 60% the pillar reads Not rated; a composite containing an unrated pillar is also suppressed.

glossary.name: Confidence weight
glossary.text: High=1.0, Medium=0.6, Low=0.3. Used to compute Weighted Evidence Adequacy.

glossary.name: Weighted evidence adequacy
glossary.text: Confidence-weighted share of scored indicators. Must clear 0.5 for the read-out to stand.

glossary.name: Stale evidence
glossary.text: A reading whose observation year is older than the indicator's max age (2 or 3 years).

glossary.name: Data Gap
glossary.text: No assessor level and no machine level. Excluded from scoring, reported separately.

glossary.name: Provisional level
glossary.text: A level derived by machine from a threshold rule, not yet confirmed by an assessor.

glossary.name: Engagement package
glossary.text: Everything assembled before the government mandate. No stage is claimable however complete the evidence looks.

methodology.purpose: DAR Studio is a working prototype of the DAMM v1.3 methodology - the diagnostic that underpins a World Bank Digital Agriculture Roadmap. It assembles what public evidence can tell us about a country's digital-agriculture readiness, shows plainly what it cannot tell us, and carries a task team through the decisions that turn a diagnostic into a roadmap.
methodology.not: It is not an official World Bank system, not a country ranking, and not a scoring service. It produces a structured basis for professional judgement; it does not replace it. Every stage it displays is provisional until a human validates the evidence behind it.

rules.title: Machines compute, humans gate
rules.text: Everything mechanical - fetching public indicators, applying threshold rules, recomputing read-outs, drafting memo narratives - is automated. Everything consequential - whether to engage, which chains to target, what the evidence means, whether to adopt - is a human decision, recorded with the role that made it. Step 1 is the machine's own step and hands over to you when it finishes; from Step 2 onwards the ladder moves only when a human records the decision.

rules.title: Three read-outs, never one number
rules.text: Capability, ecosystem and outcomes are reported separately and never averaged into a single index. A country can build strong systems before outcomes move, and a composite would hide exactly that gap - which is usually the finding that matters most for sequencing investment.

rules.title: Foundations are not tradeable
rules.text: Thirteen core-gate indicators are treated as prerequisites, not as points. A core gate at Level 1 caps the overall stage regardless of strength elsewhere, because no amount of innovation activity compensates for absent rural connectivity or a missing farmer registry.

rules.title: Silence beats a confident guess
rules.text: Where evidence is too thin, the model suppresses the score rather than computing one. A pillar below its coverage gate reads Not rated, and any composite containing it is suppressed too. An unmeasured core gate suppresses the stage entirely - so a gap can never be hidden by simply not measuring it.

rules.title: Evidence carries its provenance and its age
rules.text: Every value records where it came from. Imported readings carry their source and observation year and are marked provisional until an assessor validates them; assessor judgements record the acting role and the time they were made. Where an observation year is present and older than this model allows for that indicator, the value is flagged stale until it is refreshed.

rules.title: Nothing before the mandate is an assessment
rules.text: Work assembled before the government mandate is an engagement package - preparatory material for a Bank decision, not a judgement about the country. No maturity stage is claimable from it, however complete the evidence looks.

chain.text: Each of the indicators carries a rubric: either numeric thresholds or a written anchor per level.
Evidence yields a level from 1 to 5 - machine-suggested from a threshold, or set by an assessor, who always wins. An indicator marked as a data gap contributes nothing.
A pillar score is the plain mean of the levels assigned within it - but only if enough of its indicators are levelled to clear the coverage gate.
Capability combines its four pillar scores using the weights below; ecosystem combines its two; outcomes is a single pillar. If any member pillar is unrated, the composite is unrated.
A non-compensatory cascade turns the three read-outs into one stage, applying the gate rules and coverage thresholds first - which is why a stage can be withheld even when scores exist.

methodology.provenance: The methodology is defined in the DAMM v1.3 draft package (Framework Specification, Operator Guide, Workbook, and a Red Team & Stress Test report that returned a conditional pass for pilot preparation). The app reads it from one versioned configuration file rather than scattering it through the code. The indicator census, rubrics, pillar weights, coverage gates and confidence weights are extracted directly from the workbook's cells; the level bands and stage thresholds are transcribed from it; and the decision ladder, the prohibitions and the wording on this page are authored in that same configuration. The non-compensatory stage cascade itself lives in the scoring engine, which is regression-tested against the Bhutan worked example - that test pins the worked example and the gate behaviours, not every possible combination.

ladder.name: Automated diagnostic
ladder.guidance: The machine collects public evidence and routes named gaps to data stewards. Nothing here claims a maturity stage - it is an engagement package assembled for your Step 2 decision.

ladder.name: Engage / mode / budget
ladder.decision: Engage or defer; assessment mode; budget and team

options.name: Defer
options.means: No assessment now; the desk pack is archived and revisited when the country context or the lending pipeline changes.
options.suits: Weak government demand, no mandate prospect, or a crowded pipeline.

options.name: Rapid assessment
options.means: Desk evidence plus a short remote validation with the digital authority and the statistics office; core gates only.
options.cost: Lowest cost and counterpart burden; a narrower evidence base.
options.suits: A decision needed quickly, or a country where the desk already covers most core gates.

options.name: Standard assessment
options.means: Full indicator set with a mission, an evidence panel and a validation workshop - the mode the methodology is calibrated for.
options.cost: Highest counterpart burden; the only mode that supports a validated stage across all pillars.
options.suits: A live or imminent operation where the roadmap will inform financing.

options.name: Standard with farmer demand survey
options.means: Standard, plus the farmer demand and use survey attached to the evidence plan.
options.cost: Adds survey cost and time to the Standard mode.
options.suits: Where adoption risk is the central question and demand-side evidence is thin.

ladder.guidance: Decide whether to engage, in what assessment mode, and with what budget and team. The machine drafts the memo and frames the options; the decision - including the rejected alternatives - is yours and is recorded.

ladder.name: Targeting hypotheses
ladder.decision: Chain shortlist and segmentation to propose to government
ladder.guidance: Shortlist the value chains and segmentation to propose to government. Use the M1 targeting module in the exported workbook for the analysis; record the shortlist (and the chains you rejected) as the Step 3 decision.

ladder.name: Evidence plan & mission design
ladder.guidance: Plan how every unmeasured core gate and stale item will be evidenced, and design the mission. Each named gap already carries an authoritative steward route from Step 1.

ladder.name: Government gates
ladder.decision: Mandate letter; steering committee; endorsed chain selection
ladder.guidance: Government decides: mandate letter, steering committee, endorsed chain selection. Nothing before this step carries a stage - the engagement-package rule holds until the mandate exists.

ladder.name: Validated read-outs
ladder.guidance: The evidence panel validates the read-outs. Setting an assessor level converts machine imports to human-validated evidence; every core gate must be measured before a stage can be read out to the workshop.

ladder.name: Portfolio scenario
ladder.guidance: Assemble the portfolio scenario and envelope with finance sign-off, using the workbook's investment appraisal (unit costs, inclusion and DPI gates).

ladder.name: Adopt & disclose
ladder.guidance: Adopt the DAR, disclose it, and version the record. Export and archive the final workbook as the auditable artefact.
